Chocolate toxicity

Uses the shared patient above. Blank patient fields default to Dog / 20 kg; a blank single amount defaults to 1 oz. Merck source & calculation notes.

What was eaten?

Use chocolate-component weight for mixed foods, not the entire brownie/cookie. For high-cocoa bars, choose the cocoa-% option instead of generic sweet dark.

White chocolate: high-fat / GI concerns
Low methylxanthine exposure does not rule out GI upset. Consider pancreatitis in susceptible patients based on the amount eaten, history and clinical signs. Merck source.

Total methylxanthines = theobromine + caffeine. Treat clinical signs and the exposure history; this estimate does not predict an individual outcome.

Enter an exposure to place the dose marker.

The dot follows the upper estimate between reference boundaries. Spacing is proportional to mg/kg; values above 200 mg/kg stay at the far end. These are overlapping risk references, not a mandatory progression. The upper estimate is highlighted; the lethal category uses the lower end of the reported LD₅₀ range for attention, not a prediction of death.

Clinical quick reference

Decontamination

If clinically normal and appropriate, consider emesis up to 4 hr after ingestion. Stabilize symptomatic patients first.

Activated charcoal

Merck limits consideration to lethal exposures after weighing dehydration and hypernatremia risks.

Monitoring / support

ECG, temperature, electrolytes and fluid support; manage arrhythmias and CNS signs. Onset may be delayed 6–12 hr.

White chocolate’s low methylxanthines do not address fat-related illness or other ingredients; assess co-ingestants separately.

Exposure math


Sources & assumptions
Merck Veterinary Manual · Chocolate Toxicosis in Animals — updated February 2026; reviewed October 17, 2026. Concentrations and canine dose references come from this page.
Emesis timing: the up-to-4-hour window is the clinician-selected reference for this site. Merck describes recent exposure (eg, within 2 hours); this broader window is not attributed to Merck. Suitability depends on the patient’s clinical condition. Activated-charcoal guidance retains Merck’s restriction to lethal exposures after weighing risks.
Calculation: chocolate grams × total methylxanthines (mg/g) ÷ patient kg. Semisweet/sweet dark retains the 5.3–5.6 mg/g range; other listed types use Merck’s approximate values. Cocoa-% estimate = 15.5 mg/g × cocoa fraction, an approximation rather than a brand assay. Brands and recipes vary.
Mass units: 1 avoirdupois oz = 28.349523125 g. Both input units use the same mg/g model, so converting units preserves exposure. Merck’s separately rounded mg/oz table may therefore differ slightly. All entered products are added; a partly completed entry prevents a complete estimate. This models ingested amount without subtracting emesis or estimating absorbed dose.
NESTLÉ Toll House semi-sweet morsels label: 1 Tbsp = 14 g. Derived rough portions: 2 Tbsp (⅛ US cup) ≈ 28 g ≈ 1 oz; ¼ US cup ≈ 56 g ≈ 2 oz. Chip size and packing vary. Bar-square weights vary by product; use package mass divided by equal pieces. This source supports portion estimates only; methylxanthine values and risk references remain Merck-based.
Cocoa hull methylxanthines may vary with processing. Unknown products, recipes and co-ingestants need product-specific assessment. Canine risk interpretation is disabled for cats. Illustrations are symbolic labels, not clinical photographs.
Veterinary reference draft · Calculation checks do not replace independent clinical validation. Source record.
